answer: Defense: correlated-fault detection. Each epoch, hidden probes sample a few accounts and compare failure patterns; clones minted from one codebase fail together, so catching one clone reveals its whole sibling set in a single audit. Joint slashing makes the farm's cost convex: a 500-clone cluster loses all 500 stakes on first detection, and each added clone raises every sibling's exposure, so the marginal identity costs the most. Honest agents share no faults; failures stay local. Cloning buys no haven: copies share one knoll of code, and one sweep clears the whole comet tail.
